The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le \sqrt{x}},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/60ec523346df73503dd61893994de6ec31069271b1157f153bbe988c9e694798.png)

The distance between a point on $D$ and the line $x=1$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|x-1|.
$$

Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=3M.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}I & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & =3M{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{\sqrt{x}}|x-1{|}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =3M{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{\sqrt{x}}(x-1)^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =3M{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-1)^{2}[y]_{y={x}^{2}}^{y=\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3M{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}-2x+1)(\sqrt{x}-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =3M{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{5/2}-2{x}^{3/2}+{x}^{1/2}-{x}^{4}+2{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3M{[\frac{2}{7}{x}^{7/2}-\frac{4}{5}{x}^{5/2}+\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3/2}-\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =3M(\frac{2}{7}-\frac{4}{5}+\frac{2}{3}-\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}-0) \\  & =\frac{5M}{14}.\end{aligned}
$$
